skill.name: planning-with-files
skill.description: Uses persistent Markdown files to plan complex tasks, track progress, store research notes, and produce final deliverables.
skill.summary: Create task plans, notes, and deliverables that keep long AI work organized.
skill.author: AmmarCodes

content.user_title: Organize Complex Work with Planning Files
content.value_statement: Complex AI work can lose goals, decisions, and research details across long sessions. This skill uses persistent Markdown files to keep planning, notes, and deliverables visible.
actual_capabilities: Creates a task_plan.md structure with goals, phases, questions, decisions, errors, and status.
Uses notes.md to preserve research sources, findings, and synthesized information.
Tracks progress by updating phase checkboxes and current status after major work.
Encourages reading the plan before major decisions to keep goals current.
Defines final deliverable files for summaries, fixes, reports, or implementation notes.
limitations: It creates or updates Markdown files in the working directory.
It is unnecessary for quick questions, lookups, or small single-file edits.
It does not verify sources or facts without separate research tools.
It may require cleanup if planning files should not remain in a project.

use_cases.title: Coordinate a Bug Fix
use_cases.description: Developers can map investigation, root cause notes, implementation steps, and verification before editing code.

use_cases.title: Organize Research
use_cases.description: Analysts can store sources, compare findings, and convert notes into a structured summary.

use_cases.title: Manage Long Deliverables
use_cases.description: Writers can track drafts, decisions, blockers, and final sections across a multi-stage document.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Simple Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use planning-with-files for this task. Create a task_plan.md with the goal, phases, key questions, and current status.

prompt_templates.title: Track Research Notes
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the three-file pattern for this research task. Keep sources and findings in notes.md, then create a concise final deliverable.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Development Task
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan this implementation with task_plan.md. Record decisions, errors, files investigated, and verification steps before delivering the result.

prompt_templates.title: Recover and Continue a Long Task
prompt_templates.prompt: Read the existing task_plan.md and notes.md. Reconstruct the current state, update the plan, then continue from the next incomplete phase.

output_examples.input: Research a topic and produce a summary.
output: A task plan with research phases and current status.
A notes file with source names and synthesized findings.
A final summary file that references the saved notes.

output_examples.input: Fix a login defect in an application.
output: A plan showing investigation, root cause, implementation, and test phases.
Decision notes about the relevant files and suspected failure point.
A completion summary with verification results and remaining risks.

best_practices: Use the pattern only when a task has several phases or needs saved context.
Read the plan before major decisions and update it after completed phases.
Keep sensitive details out of planning files unless the workspace is trusted.
anti_patterns: Creating planning files for simple questions or quick one-step tasks.
Storing large notes without linking them to the task goal.
Leaving status, errors, or decisions stale after important changes.

faq.question: Does it run shell commands?
faq.answer: No. The examples describe agent file operations, not required shell execution.

faq.question: Which files does it use?
faq.answer: It centers on task_plan.md, notes.md, and a final deliverable Markdown file.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow is plain Markdown and fits Claude, Codex, and Claude Code sessions.

faq.question: When should I skip it?
faq.answer: Skip it for quick answers, simple lookups, and small single-file edits.

faq.question: Will it verify research sources?
faq.answer: No. It stores sources and findings, but source quality still depends on the tools and review process.

faq.question: Can I resume work later?
faq.answer: Yes. Read the plan and notes first, then continue from the next incomplete phase.
